title: Usage
text: gruntz_limit(f, x, x0 = Inf; dir = :+, build = nothing, lift = nothing) computes . The limit point x0 may be Inf, -Inf, a number, or an expression that does not contain x. For a finite x0, dir chooses the side the limit is taken from: :+ (from the right, the default), :- (from the left), or :both …

title: SymEngine
text:
With SymEngine, create the variable (and any parameters) with @vars. Then write the expression as you normally would. using GruntzLimit
using SymEngine
@vars x a

gruntz_limit(sin(x)/x, x, 0)1  Limits at infinity are the default: gruntz_limit(x^2 * exp(-x), x)0  gruntz_limit(sqrt(x^2 + x) - x, …

title: Julia Expr
text:
TermInterface.jl defines iscall, operation and arguments for Julia's Expr, so a quoted expression works without any symbolic package. The variable is passed as a Symbol: using GruntzLimit

gruntz_limit(:(sin(x)/x), :x, 0)1  gruntz_limit(:(1/x^2 - 1/sin(x)^2), :x, 0)-1//3  gruntz_limit(:(x/abs(x)), …

title: Expr answers
text: For Expr input, a non-rational answer is returned as an unevaluated Expr, so it stays exact and may contain parameters: gruntz_limit(:((1 + 1/x)^x), :x):(exp(1))  gruntz_limit(:((1 + a/x)^x), :x):(exp(a))  gruntz_limit(:(sqrt(x^2 + a*x) - x), :x):(1//2 * a)  L = gruntz_limit(:(atan(1/x)), :x, 0; …

title: Supported functions

title: When there is no limit
text:
A GruntzError is also thrown when the limit does not exist. For example, bounded oscillation: try
    gruntz_limit(sin(x), x)
catch err
    err
endGruntzError("argument of exp/sin/cos diverges (oscillation or essential singularity)")  or one-sided limits that disagree, with dir = :both: try

title: How it works
text: This is an outline of Gruntz's algorithm as implemented here. Gruntz's thesis has the details and proofs.

title: Reduction to
text: Every limit is reduced to a limit at : : substitute ;: substitute ;: substitute ;dir = :both computes both one-sided limits and checks that they agree. As , each expression handled here eventually has a constant sign. So abs(u) is replaced by sign(u) * u before the limit is computed.

title: Canonical form
text: The input term is converted into an internal canonical form: sums of monomials with exact rational coefficients and exponents, built over atoms. text: A rational answer is returned as an Int or Rational, and an infinite one as ±Inf. Anything else is converted back from the canonical form by calling build(op, args...) for each compound node, and lift for each number.
